Charge, spin, orbital and lattice degrees of freedom are simultaneously active and strongly coupled in many quantum materials, and their competition and cooperation can give rise to complex ordered phases\ucitedagottoComplexityStronglyCorrelated2005. A broad range of collective excitations and characteristic gaps lie in the THz and MIR range\ucitebasovElectrodynamicsCorrelated2011. Linear spectroscopy determines their resonance energies, oscillator strengths, linewidths and selection rules, but interactions among different excitations can remain difficult to disentangle in a one-dimensional spectrum\uciteliuMultidimensionalTerahertzProbes2025. Nonlinear measurements provide access to harmonic generation, wave mixing, multidimensional correlations and phase-sensitive observables, which can reveal mode coupling, coherent pathways and symmetry constraints\ucitehuang_terahertz_2026.
